character: Pacifidlog floats: its Pokemon fish, smoke the catch, bail, caulk and keep the lights on the rafts, and the rest are the sea's, washed up on doorsteps, in the bait tanks, on the breakwater and tied up alongside. Water Pokemon only, and the only town with no ground under it: every y here is the deck's (walk y63), never the heightmap's sea floor.

workers.interact: The Kingler brings the Row's catch to the guild held high in its big claw. It has never dropped one, and never let go of one either.
The Veluza hangs the catch in the smokehouse, cleaned. Nobody asks how it cleans them so fast.
The Bruxish leaps off the Row and comes back up grinning with a fish. Do not look at its head for too long.
The Dhelmise holds the new hull's keel steady while the boatwright fits the ribs. It knows a great deal about hulls, mostly from the bottom.
The Barbaracle caulks the hull's seams with seven hands, and argues with itself about every one.
The Marill is bailing out the moored raft with its tail. The raft is not leaking. The Marill likes bailing.
The Floatzel watches the Current Gate's water. It has pulled out three swimmers this month and is waiting for the fourth.
The Spheal rolls the Mart's barrels round to the back on its nose. It has dropped one in the sea and does not want to talk about it.
The Chinchou is the centre raft's night light. On a dark night it blinks to the boats coming in.
The Piplup polishes the guild's catch board every morning. It stands on tiptoe to do the top line, which is still empty.
The Oshawott opens clams for the Row's stall with its scalchop. It checks each one for a pearl first.
The Buizel scrubs the raft's logs by spinning on them. The deck is very clean and slightly worn.
The Poliwhirl winds the stilt quarter's mooring ropes round the landing post. It goes round the way the spiral on its belly goes.

pets.why: the square counter's Shellos, which is the wrong colour for this side of the sea and is very proud of it
the counter clerk's Popplio, which blows a bubble at every customer
the Row stall-keeper's Totodile, which has bitten every fisher in town once, affectionately
the Row stall's Sobble, half-hidden behind the fish crates; it cries when anyone haggles

in a bucket by the square counter; the clerk swears it is a pet and not stock. Re-homed 2026-10-06 from pacifidlog_fishers_row (it was in a bucket by the Row stall): the Row keeper's ring has room for two of his three pets (the clam workers and the stall take the rest), and the market's speaker beside him is not an NPC the town plan knows

placed.why: on the Centre's red roof, the highest perch on the rafts
in the Centre's gutter in its bubble, where the rain refills it
flat on the Mart's step like a doormat; customers wipe their feet beside it, not on it
in the Centre's window, in the nurse's jar
beside the step of the hut on raft 3; the family keeps it watered
by the step of the hut on raft 7; it shuts when anyone walks past
on the doorstep of the hut on raft 2, where it washes up every morning; somebody throws it back every evening
flapping beside the step of the hut on raft 8, where it has flapped for a week and is fine
beside the step of the hut on raft 11, holding the door's latch string in its shell

situations.title: The Lapras tied up at the guild raft
situations.story: A Lapras is tied up alongside the guild raft like a boat, and a Froakie and a Quaxly sit on its back as if it were part of the deck. Nobody remembers tying it.
situations.why: Pacifidlog's own: a town on the water moors what it has; on the guild raft's north edge, the Lapras in the water beside it

situations.title: The bait tanks on the Row
situations.story: The Row keeps its bait in a row of tanks, and the tanks are full of Wishiwashi. The fishers have stopped using them as bait. One day there will be enough of them.
situations.why: a school IS the situation; along the Row's south edge near its root

situations.title: The one that got away
situations.story: A Seaking lies on the guild raft beside the catch board, with a Goldeen. The fishers measure it every day. It is never caught, and the board's top line stays empty.
situations.why: by the guild hall's west wall, where the catch board is

situations.title: The flock on the breakwater
situations.story: Three Flamigo stand on the Current Gate's breakwater on one leg each, facing the current. They move in step, and nobody has seen them start.
situations.why: a flock IS the situation; on the breakwater by the gate

situations.title: Why nobody swims at the gate
situations.story: A Mareanie and a Toxapex live on the swimmers' hut's ladder. The hut still has a sign that says Swimmers. Nobody swims at the Current Gate any more.
situations.why: the swimmers' hut on the gate raft

situations.title: The sushi on the inn's tray
situations.story: A Tatsugiri has lain on the inn's serving tray by the door all week, pretending to be sushi. A Carvanha waits beside it, hungry and not fooled.
situations.why: on the stilt boardwalk at the inn's door

situations.title: The angler who uses its tail
situations.story: A Slowpoke sits at the edge of the south raft with its tail in the sea. It has fished there since spring and caught nothing, and the fishers have started leaving it the odd sardine so it does not lose heart.
situations.why: a fishing town's laziest fisher: on the south raft's west edge at the deck's walk y 63, the open sea one block west (the plan's seabed at x 5159). Slowpoke is 1.2 wide, so it takes the three deck cells x 5160-5162, z 7420-7422; the barrel is the sardines

situations.title: One sheet too many
situations.story: There is washing out on the line at the north edge of the raft, two sheets and something between them. Nobody hung out a third sheet. It is a Frillish, and it has been drying for a week.
situations.why: a raft town's washing line over the water, on the north edge of the raft at x 5138-5152 (deck walk y 63, the sea at z 7417 west of x 5140): a Frillish is the one Pokemon that reads as a wet sheet

situations.title: The lamp that came back on
situations.story: The lamp-keeper put up a bare post where the boardwalk meets the west raft, meaning to finish the lamp in the morning. That night a Starmie climbed onto it and lit it, and it has lit it every night since. The lamp-keeper has stopped ordering the glass.
situations.why: the boardwalk's lamps stand on its north and south edges every 8 blocks in turn (the last north one at x 4995, the last south one at 4987); its west end meets the west raft at x 4980, on whose north edge (deck walk y 63) the Starmie's post stands. Pacifidlog keeps the lights, and this one keeps itself
